text:
maria_sales: Quick Acme POC network ask — they need to preserve client source IP for audit logs when calls from their app hit our Private deployment. Considering PrivateLink vs VPC peering + NAT. Any quick guidance? cc @sam_se @jon_netops

sam_se: Short answer: PrivateLink (backed by NLB) preserves source IP. VPC peering also preserves IP. Anything that NATs or proxies (terminating TLS) will replace it. @jon_netops can add SNI/proxy details. :ok_hand:

jon_netops: Agree. A few practical notes:
- PrivateLink + NLB -> original client IP is preserved (NLB preserves src ip).
- If we put an ALB or TLS-terminating proxy in front, the source IP will be the proxy.
- NAT Gateway / Internet Gateway + SNAT will show NAT EIP, not client IP.

maria_sales: Got it — if Acme needs original IP in their logs we should recommend PrivateLink with NLB or VPC peering. Any firewall/ports checklist I can hand them?

jon_netops: Short checklist for customer network team:
- Outbound: TCP 443 to our PrivateLink endpoint ENIs (vpce-*) OR to our published EIP(s) if peering/IGW is used.
- Health checks: NLB health checks run on the service port (usually 443) — ensure target accepts TCP on that port.
- If they use TLS inspection or an SNI proxy, confirm the proxy does NOT SNAT, or accept that logs will show proxy IP.
- If they need static egress IPs, recommend BYO-EIP or a NAT with fixed EIP.

Example SG/egress snippet for their firewall team:
```
Type: Egress
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Destination: vpce-xxxxxxxx (PrivateLink) OR 34.56.78.90/32 (our dedicated EIP)
```

sam_se: Pricing note: PrivateLink adds AWS endpoint hourly + data processing charges. Also mention our Private deployment/network egress pricing on the quote. I'll ping revenue to get a quick ballpark for Acme.

alex_finance: We typically show: PrivateLink endpoint cost + ~$0.02–0.09/GB data processing (depends on region) + our egress line item if applicable. I'll draft a ballpark and attach to the POC quote.

amanda_security: From the security questionnaire: they asked about KMS/HSM and audit logs. PrivateLink itself doesn't change compliance. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS integration and can stream audit logs to their SIEM via our logging endpoint. I'll send the standard sec answers.

maria_sales: Follow-up from Acme: can we support an SNI proxy in transit (TLS passthrough) while still preserving client IP? They want TLS inspection but keep original IPs in app logs.

jon_netops: If the proxy is TLS passthrough (i.e., SNI routing only, no TLS terminate), client IP is preserved because the TCP connection is end-to-end. If the proxy terminates TLS (MITM/TLS-inspect), source IP becomes the proxy unless the proxy forwards original IP via PROXY protocol or X-Forwarded-For and the backend is configured to parse it. We support PROXY protocol (v1/v2) on our NLB — recommend that if they must terminate TLS.

sam_se: Important ops note: we can enable PROXY protocol on the NLB to preserve client IP in cases where a proxy terminates TLS. Customer must configure their proxy/backend to emit/consume PROXY headers. We'll add this to the runbook.

deploybot: deploy-checklist: created NET-ACME-042 for endpoint provisioning, tagging, and optional EIP allocation.

maria_sales: Perfect — I'll capture these items in the POC runbook and loop in Acme's NetOps (Priya). Thanks all :thumbsup:
